text:
sara: FYI - next week we're doing the Atlassian cloud cutover for Jira & Confluence (Atlassian Access + SCIM + OIDC). This is the migration we've been planning since Q4.

sara: High level: we'll move projects/spaces from self-hosted -> Atlassian Cloud org, enable SCIM for account provisioning, switch SSO to OIDC via our IdP bridge, and update webhooks/integrations to the cloud endpoints.

sara: Timeline (rolled up):
- Wed 2025-02-12 22:00 UTC: dry-run migration for staging org (no downtime)
- Thu 2025-02-13 02:00-04:00 UTC: blue/green cutover for non-critical projects (low traffic)
- Sat 2025-02-15 01:00-05:00 UTC: org-wide cutover window (expected ~2-3h for final sync)

leo: What should owners do now?

sara: Owners please: add your project to the migration spreadsheet, confirm a rollback contact, and validate the team mappings in the Groups sheet. Default deadline is EOD Mon 2025-02-10.

priya: Any changes to API tokens or service accounts we should expect?

sara: Yes - cloud requires scoped API tokens and deprecates legacy basic auth. We'll rotate service-account credentials: create a new cloud-service SA in IAM, then provision a scoped API token via the Atlassian UI. We'll publish a small script to fetch and store tokens in Vault. Old tokens will be revoked after 14 days.

oscar: How will SCIM handle group names? We have a bunch of teams with special characters.

sara: SCIM mapping rules will normalize names (lowercase, dashes). We'll add an allowlist for exceptions. If you have a group that must keep exact name, mark it in the spreadsheet and we'll create an alias mapping.

priya: What about automation rules and webhooks? A lot of our automations post to internal endpoints.

sara: Webhooks will need to be updated to use cloud URL patterns. We'll provide a migration proxy for 7 days post-cutover: requests to old webhook URLs will be forwarded and logged so teams can flip endpoints without immediate breakage. Also note that webhook payload shape for some events changes (issue.updated -> issue:updated in a few automations). We'll publish a delta mapping doc.

platform-bot: [notice] staging dry-run scheduled: 2025-02-12T22:00:00Z. Runbook: https://internal.redwood.dev/platform/jira-confluence-cutover-runbook

leo: Are there any SSO changes devs need to do? Will they need to re-auth?

sara: Users will re-authorize the Atlassian cloud app once SSO is switched. We'll enable Just-In-Time provisioning so new accounts are created automatically. For existing users we will map by primary email; if your account uses alternate email please file an exception.

oscar: How will historical audit logs be handled? We need to retain them for compliance.

sara: We will export on-prem audit logs to S3 and surface them in the central audit index. Retention for exported logs will be 3 years. Cloud provides its own audit logs too; we'll stream those to our SIEM.

priya: Can we test the OIDC flow locally? Example curl to exchange code for token?

sara: Yep - example (staging):

```
# exchange code for tokens against our IdP bridge
curl -X POST "https://idp.internal/oauth2/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d 'grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=cloud-app&code=CODE&redirect_uri=https://staging-atlassian.cloud/_oauth/callback'
```

sara: We'll also provide a short test harness repo (github.com/redwood/platform-atlassian-tests) that runs an end-to-end create->transition->webhook assert.

leo: If we find an issue, is there a rollback plan?

sara: Yes - rollback options:
- flip DNS to the old proxy endpoints (5-10m)
- re-enable on-prem Jira as read-write in failover mode (30-60m, but data may need re-sync)
- migrator-bot can pause the final sync step if we detect high error rates.

migrator-bot: [alert] final-sync pause toggle available at https://migrator.internal/ops/12345 (requires platform-admin role)

oscar: Will automation tokens stored in Vault be rotated automatically?

sara: We'll rotate Vault-stored tokens using a small controller that writes new tokens into path secret/atlassian/<repo>. Teams that use the tokens via CI should reference that path. We'll post an example GH Action that reads from Vault using OIDC.

priya: Anything special for mobile clients / mobile SSO?

sara: Mobile clients will hit the same OIDC flow; make sure mobile SSO redirect URIs are registered in the IdP bridge. If you maintain an internal mobile app that uses embedded webviews, file a ticket so we can whitelist it.

leo: Are we changing Jira project keys during migration? That could break a lot of links.

sara: We will preserve project keys exactly where possible. Where a conflict exists (same key in cloud), we'll append _LEGACY to the old one and then migrate issues. We'll document any changes and create redirect aliases in our link-resolution service.

platform-bot: [reminder] owners: confirm entries in migration spreadsheet by 2025-02-10 23:59 PT.

sara: OK - final callouts: backlog import may be ~10-15% slower during final sync window; communications to customers will go out via #customers and product comms. Schedule a 15-min pre-cutover check-in (UTC) with the platform ops lead if you're in the pilot list.

leo: I'll add core-platform and infra-alerting projects to the staging dry-run.

priya: Thanks - I'll validate automation tokens and webhook payloads.

oscar: I'll validate our Confluence templates and flag any external embeds.

sara: Thanks all. Runbook link again: https://internal.redwood.dev/platform/jira-confluence-cutover-runbook. Ping me or @platform if anything is urgent.
